claims.text: Sarcoidosis: other immunosuppressants are used when
claims.quote: Other immunosuppressants are used when

claims.text: prednisone is not tolerated,
claims.quote: Patients cannot tolerate prednisone

claims.text: disease is refractory to moderate–high dose prednisone,
claims.quote: Sarcoidosis is refractory to moderate to high doses of prednisone

claims.text: or prednisone can't be tapered below 10–15 mg/day after 3 months.
claims.quote: Prednisone dose cannot be tapered below 10 to 15 mg daily after 3 months

claims.text: Methotrexate is the most commonly used;
claims.quote: Methotrexate is the most commonly used immunosuppressant.

claims.text: 6-month trial of 10–15 mg/week.
claims.quote: Patients should be given a 6-month trial of methotrexate 10 to 15 mg/week.

claims.text: Start with the corticosteroid, then taper the steroid over 6–8 weeks (often stopped);
claims.quote: Initially, methotrexate and corticosteroids are both given; over 6 to 8 weeks, the corticosteroid dose can be tapered and, in many cases, stopped.

claims.text: maximal MTX response may take 6–12 months, so taper prednisone more slowly in those cases.
claims.quote: The maximal response to methotrexate, however, may take 6 to 12 months. In such cases, prednisone must be tapered more slowly.

claims.text: Relapse is common after stopping an immunosuppressant.
claims.quote: Relapse is common after stopping an immunosuppressant.

claims.text: Test for HBV and HCV before starting.
claims.quote: Before starting methotrexate, patients should be tested for hepatitis B virus and hepatitis C virus infection.

claims.text: CBC and liver enzymes every 2–4 weeks initially, then every 6–12 weeks once the dose is stable.
claims.quote: Serial blood counts and liver enzyme tests should be done every 2 to 4 weeks initially and then every 6 to 12 weeks once a stable dose is achieved.

claims.text: CI: pregnancy (non-neoplastic disease);
claims.quote: For non-neoplastic diseases, methotrexate tablets are contraindicated in pregnancy.

claims.text: history of severe hypersensitivity incl. anaphylaxis.
claims.quote: Methotrexate tablets are contraindicated in patients with a history of severe hypersensitivity reactions to methotrexate, including anaphylaxis

claims.text: Verify pregnancy status before starting.
claims.quote: Verify pregnancy status in females of reproductive potential before starting TREXALL

claims.text: Boxed warning: embryo-fetal toxicity, hypersensitivity, severe ADRs, medication errors.
claims.quote: WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY, HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTIONS, SEVERE ADVERSE REACTIONS, AND RISK OF MEDICATION ERRORS

claims.text: Serious ADRs incl. death (bone marrow, GI, liver, lungs, skin, kidneys).
claims.quote: Serious adverse reactions, including death, have been reported with methotrexate. Closely monitor for adverse reactions of the bone marrow, gastrointestinal tract, liver, lungs, skin, and kidneys.
claims.locator: Boxed Warning: Embryo-Fetal Toxicity, Hypersensitivity Reactions, Severe Adverse Reactions, and Risk of Medication Errors

claims.text: Myelosuppression can be severe (pancytopenia).
claims.quote: TREXALL suppresses hematopoiesis and can cause severe and life-threatening pancytopenia, anemia, leukopenia, neutropenia, and thrombocytopenia

claims.text: Hepatotoxicity (fibrosis, cirrhosis),
claims.quote: TREXALL can cause severe and potentially irreversible hepatotoxicity, including fibrosis, cirrhosis, and fatal liver failure

claims.text: higher risk with heavy alcohol use.
claims.quote: The risk of hepatotoxicity is increased with heavy alcohol consumption.

claims.text: Pulmonary toxicity: acute or chronic interstitial pneumonitis, can be irreversible or fatal.
claims.quote: Pulmonary toxicity, including acute or chronic interstitial pneumonitis and irreversible or fatal cases, can occur with TREXALL

claims.text: Severe skin reactions (SJS/TEN).
claims.quote: Severe, including fatal dermatologic reactions, such as toxic epidermal necrolysis, Stevens- Johnson syndrome, exfoliative dermatitis, skin necrosis, and erythema multiforme, can occur with TREXALL

claims.text: Renal toxicity.
claims.quote: TREXALL can cause renal toxicity, including irreversible acute renal failure

claims.text: ↑ MTX levels/toxicity with:
claims.quote: Coadministration of methotrexate with the following products may increase methotrexate plasma concentrations, which may increase the risk of methotrexate severe adverse reactions.
claims.locator: 7.1 Effects of Other Drugs on Methotrexate

claims.text: aspirin & other NSAIDs;
claims.quote: Aspirin and other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
claims.locator: 7.1 Effects of Other Drugs on Methotrexate

claims.text: penicillins & sulfonamides
claims.quote: Oral or intravenous penicillin or sulfonamide antibiotics
claims.locator: 7.1 Effects of Other Drugs on Methotrexate

claims.text: (incl. other antifolates);
claims.quote: Antifolate drugs (e.g., dapsone, pemetrexed, pyrimethamine and sulfonamides)
claims.locator: 7.1 Effects of Other Drugs on Methotrexate

claims.text: PPIs;
claims.quote: Proton pump inhibitors
claims.locator: 7.1 Effects of Other Drugs on Methotrexate

claims.text: probenecid.
claims.quote: Probenecid
claims.locator: 7.1 Effects of Other Drugs on Methotrexate

claims.text: Avoid nitrous oxide anesthesia.
claims.quote: Avoid nitrous oxide anesthesia in patients receiving methotrexate.
claims.locator: 7.1 Effects of Other Drugs on Methotrexate

claims.text: Take once WEEKLY as a single dose: taking the weekly dose daily has caused fatal toxicity.
claims.quote: advise patients and caregivers that the recommended dosage is to be taken once weekly as a single dose and that mistakenly taking the recommended weekly dosage once daily has led to fatal adverse reactions

claims.text: Avoid excess sun; use sun protection.
claims.quote: Advise patients to avoid excessive sun exposure and use sun protection measures.

claims.text: Live vaccines not recommended.
claims.quote: Immunizations with live vaccines is not recommended.

claims.text: Do not breastfeed.
claims.quote: Lactation : Instruct not to breastfeed.

claims.text: Overdose: leucovorin (or levoleucovorin) as soon as possible,
claims.quote: Administer leucovorin or levoleucovorin as soon as possible after TREXALL overdosage).

claims.text: guided by serum creatinine and MTX levels.
claims.quote: Monitor serum creatinine and methotrexate levels to guide leucovorin or levoleucovorin therapy.

claims.text: Glucarpidase for toxic MTX levels (> 1 µmol/L) with delayed clearance from renal impairment.
claims.quote: Glucarpidase is indicated for the treatment of toxic plasma methotrexate concentrations (>1 micromole per liter) in patients with delayed methotrexate clearance due to impaired renal function.

claims.text: Sarcoidosis: nonbiologic immunosuppressant option;
claims.quote: Other nonbiologic immunosuppressants include azathioprine, mycophenolate, cyclophosphamide, leflunomide, and hydroxychloroquine.

claims.text: usually effective for hypercalcemia, arthralgia, skin sarcoidosis, or enlarged uncomfortable/disfiguring peripheral lymph nodes.
claims.quote: Hydroxychloroquine is usually effective for treating hypercalcemia, arthralgia, skin sarcoidosis, or enlarged uncomfortable or disfiguring peripheral lymph nodes.

claims.text: Eye exam before starting and every 12 months for ocular toxicity.
claims.quote: Ophthalmologic evaluation should be done before hydroxychloroquine is started and then every 12 months during treatment to monitor for its ocular toxicity.

claims.text: CI: hypersensitivity to 4-aminoquinolines.
claims.quote: PLAQUENIL is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to 4-aminoquinoline compounds.

claims.text: Avoid with congenital/acquired QT prolongation or QT risk factors.
claims.quote: Avoid PLAQUENIL administration in patients with congenital or documented acquired QT prolongation and/or known risk factors for prolongation of the QT interval

claims.text: Cardiomyopathy and ventricular arrhythmias, can be fatal;
claims.quote: Fatal or life-threatening cardiomyopathy and ventricular arrhythmias were reported.

claims.text: QT prolongation, torsades.
claims.quote: PLAQUENIL has a potential to prolong the QT interval. Ventricular arrhythmias (including torsades de pointes) have been reported in PLAQUENIL-treated patients.

claims.text: Irreversible retinal damage related to cumulative dose and duration.
claims.quote: Irreversible retinal damage is related to cumulative dosage and treatment duration.

claims.text: Severe hypoglycemia, with or without antidiabetic drugs.
claims.quote: PLAQUENIL can cause severe and potentially life-threatening hypoglycemia, in the presence or absence of antidiabetic agents

claims.text: Hemolysis in G6PD deficiency.
claims.quote: Hemolysis has been reported in patients with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency.
claims.locator: 5.7 Hemolytic Anemia Associated with G6PD Deficiency

claims.text: Not recommended with other QT-prolonging or arrhythmogenic drugs.
claims.quote: PLAQUENIL is not recommended in patients taking other drugs that have the potential to prolong the QT interval or are arrhythmogenic
claims.locator: 7.1 Drugs Prolonging QT Interval and Other Arrhythmogenic Drugs

claims.text: Overdose: onset within 1–3 h;
claims.quote: PLAQUENIL overdosage symptoms have an onset within 1–3 hours of ingestion.

claims.text: cardiovascular toxicity (QRS/QTc prolongation, VT/VF, torsades, AV block, cardiac arrest).
claims.quote: Cardiovascular toxicity, including QRS or QTc prolongation, ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, torsade de pointes, atrioventricular block, cardiac arrest and death.

claims.text: Sarcoidosis: nonbiologic immunosuppressant option (with mycophenolate, cyclophosphamide, leflunomide, HCQ).
claims.quote: Other nonbiologic immunosuppressants include azathioprine, mycophenolate, cyclophosphamide, leflunomide, and hydroxychloroquine.

claims.text: Sarcoidosis: nonbiologic immunosuppressant option (with azathioprine, mycophenolate, cyclophosphamide, HCQ).
claims.quote: Other nonbiologic immunosuppressants include azathioprine, mycophenolate, cyclophosphamide, leflunomide, and hydroxychloroquine.
